summary: There are unambiguously TWO complete frontends being served in production: the v3 token-native SPA at /app (static/v3/, ~6k lines of vanilla ES modules, the post-login destination per static/scripts/account.js:165) and a full legacy multi-page "v2.0 Platform / Workspace OS" (~17k+ lines) still mounted at /chat, /graph, /workspace, /onboarding, /admin, /agents, /workflows, /plugins/sdk, and /activity with its own nav, IA, and CSS system. The v3 SPA itself is high quality — one declarative IA table, a disciplined two-layer token system, an honest live/unavailable API adapter that never fabricates data — but the flagship "Knowledge Graph" explorer in v3 is a static SVG that is strictly weaker than the legacy force-directed canvas in static/scripts/graph.js, which is backwards for a Knowledge-Graph-First product. For v4, the legacy stack should be deleted with redirects, the canvas graph ported into the SPA as the primary surface, and the CDN font/icon dependencies removed to make the privacy-first claim true.
strengths: Single declarative IA table (static/v3/js/core/routes.js:26-67) drives the nav rail, command palette, router, breadcrumbs, and lazy view loading — one source of truth with Basic/Advanced/Admin mode gating and explicit hidden legacy routes.

Disciplined two-layer design-token system: static/css/tokens.css is the color single source (light + [data-lt-theme=dark] + OS-follow) and static/v3/css/lattice.tokens.css adds structural tokens (4pt spacing, type scale, radii, motion, rails); v3 CSS contains only ~7 raw hex occurrences vs 104 in legacy css/reference/chat.css alone — the token rule is actually followed.

Honest data layer: static/v3/js/core/api.js returns {ok, data, source: live|unavailable} for every call, never fabricates counters, and tests/unit/test_static_release_hygiene.py:57 enforces that the old fake-data fixtures.js stays deleted; views render explicit empty/unavailable states (e.g. knowledge-graph.js:148-149, planning.js header comment).

No-framework SPA is small and fast: lazy view modules, content-hashed asset build (scripts/build_v3_assets.mjs) with manifest version sourced from package.json, command palette (Cmd+K), aria labels on inputs/toggles, skip-link, mobile drawer + scrim.

The v3.6.0 knowledge-graph view (static/v3/js/views/knowledge-graph.js) has the right product framing for a Digital Brain: Explore / Status / Sources(provenance) / Capture(web URL) / Backup(export-import-backup) tabs, all wired to real endpoints.

STYLE_SYSTEM.md and FIGMA_SPEC.md are honest engineering docs — they admit there is no Figma source of truth, document the broken Vercel deployment, and record known a11y/i18n gaps instead of hiding them.

problems.title: Two complete competing frontends are both served in production
problems.detail: Login (static/scripts/account.js:165,208,226) sends users to the v3 SPA at /app, but a full parallel legacy app remains mounted: /chat → chat.html (844 lines + 5081-line scripts/chat.js), /graph and /knowledge-graph → graph.html (knowledge_graph_api.py:41-52), /workspace and /onboarding → workspace.html (latticeai/api/workspace.py:202-216), /admin → legacy admin.html (static_routes.py:121-128), /agents (agents.py:96), /workflows (workflow_designer.py:77), /plugins/sdk (plugins.py:55), /activity (realtime.py:41). workspace.html carries a complete second IA — its own rail, its own Basic/Advanced/Admin mode switcher, links to /chat, /graph, /admin — and platform.js exports a second NAV header (v2.0 Platform). Result: two chats, two graph explorers, two admin consoles, two dashboards. Legacy pages never link back to /app, so a user who lands on /workspace or /admin is trapped in the deprecated product with diverging features.

problems.title: Onboarding and /admin route new users into the legacy stack
problems.detail: GET /onboarding serves legacy workspace.html (latticeai/api/workspace.py:210-216) and GET /admin serves legacy admin.html (latticeai/api/static_routes.py:121-128), even though the v3 SPA has its own six admin views (admin-users/permissions/audit/security/policies/private-vpc). The first-run experience and the most privileged surface both bypass the product the company says is primary.

problems.title: The KG-first flagship explorer is weaker than the legacy graph page
problems.detail: v3's Knowledge Graph Explore tab renders a static SVG with a golden-spiral fallback layout (static/v3/js/views/knowledge-graph.js:147-172, layout() at 480-499) — no zoom, no pan, no drag, no physics, capped inspector list of 60. The deprecated static/scripts/graph.js (1804 lines) has a real force simulation with drag and kinetic-energy animation (lines 172-187, 893-920, 1062). For a product whose identity is 'your digital brain', the best graph UX lives in the stack slated for deletion.

problems.title: CDN dependencies contradict the privacy-first/local-first promise
problems.detail: Every page — including the v3 shell (static/v3/index.html:21-24) and login (static/account.html:13-16) — loads Inter from fonts.googleapis.com and Tabler icons from cdn.jsdelivr.net. The KG Capture tab tells users 'Nothing is sent to a cloud service' (knowledge-graph.js:352) while the page itself phones two third-party CDNs on every load and breaks entirely offline. The jsdelivr URL pins '@latest', so the icon font can silently change under the product.

problems.title: Service worker is stale and precaches the legacy app, not v3
problems.detail: static/sw.js uses cache name 'ltcai-v310' (predates 3.6.0) and its STATIC precache list is the legacy bundle — /workspace, scripts/chat.js, scripts/admin.js, scripts/graph.js, css/reference/* — plus /app's HTML shell but none of the hashed v3 JS/CSS the manifest points to. PWA offline mode therefore resurrects the deprecated UI while /app fails offline. The header comment claims cache-first for static assets but the fetch handler is network-first for everything (lines 39-71).

problems.title: ~17,000+ lines of dead/duplicated legacy frontend code, locked in by old test suites
problems.detail: Legacy surface: scripts/chat.js 5081, css/reference/chat.css 4623, scripts/graph.js 1804, css/reference/base.css 1661, scripts/admin.js 1614, workspace.css 1121, css/reference/graph.css 1016, scripts/workspace.js 948, css/responsive.css 861, css/reference/admin.css 610, plus 8 HTML pages, platform.js/platform.css and account.css. None of it is reachable from the v3 SPA. Playwright suites tests/visual/v223-v227.spec.js and qa.spec.js exist specifically to keep these v2.2.x pages working, actively taxing every future change.

problems.title: Generated hashed build artifacts are committed next to sources
problems.detail: All 38 hashed siblings (e.g. static/v3/js/views/chat.e6dd7dd0.js) plus asset-manifest.json are checked in alongside their sources, doubling the v3 file tree. They differ from sources only by rewritten import paths (verified by diff), so any source edit without re-running scripts/build_v3_assets.mjs ships a stale UI; nothing in CI verifies manifest-source consistency.

problems.title: Design-token rule is unenforced by tooling
problems.detail: scripts/lint_v3.mjs only runs `node --check` (syntax) on v3 modules. The 'never hard-code a hex for a themed surface' rule stated at the top of both token files and in STYLE_SYSTEM.md §2 has no lint backing it; the discipline currently survives on convention alone. No axe/a11y pass runs in CI either (acknowledged in STYLE_SYSTEM.md:169).

problems.title: Login page loads the entire legacy CSS system; i18n is split
problems.detail: static/account.html:17-23 pulls base.css + account.css + admin.css + graph.css + chat.css (~8,300 lines of reference CSS) to style one login form — the entry door to /app is styled by the deprecated system. Language is inconsistent: legacy pages and the invite-gate block screen (static_routes.py:61-70) are Korean-first, while the v3 SPA is English-only with stray Korean strings (acknowledged in STYLE_SYSTEM.md:175). Also inconsistent page auth: /chat is served without require_user (static_routes.py:107-109) while /graph and /workspace require it.

opportunities.title: Delete the legacy frontend and redirect its routes into /app
opportunities.detail: Remove chat.html, graph.html, workspace.html, admin.html, agents.html, workflows.html, plugins.html, activity.html, scripts/{chat,graph,workspace,admin,platform,ux}.js, workspace.css, platform.css, css/responsive.css, and css/reference/* (~17k lines). Replace the page-serving handlers in static_routes.py, workspace.py, agents.py, plugins.py, workflow_designer.py, realtime.py, knowledge_graph_api.py with 307 redirects to /app#/<route> (e.g. /graph → /app#/knowledge-graph, /workspace → /app#/home, /admin → /app#/admin/users). Retire tests/visual/v22*.spec.js and qa.spec.js with them. This collapses the product to ONE frontend and is the single highest-leverage v4 change — mostly deletion.

opportunities.title: Make the Knowledge Graph the literal primary surface with a real interactive canvas
opportunities.detail: Port the force-directed simulation, drag, and kinetic animation from static/scripts/graph.js (lines 172-1062) into the v3 Explore tab as a canvas renderer with zoom/pan, neighborhood expansion, type/source/time filters, and provenance overlay (click node → its ingestion record from /api/knowledge-graph/provenance). Make knowledge-graph the default route after login (router fallback 'home' → 'knowledge-graph' in shell.js:39) so opening the app means opening your brain. Keep the honest unavailable states.

opportunities.title: Restructure the IA around the Digital Brain mental model
opportunities.detail: Reshape routes.js groups from Workspace/Data/Retrieval/Compute/Platform/System into brain-centric pillars: Brain (Knowledge Graph — default), Ask (chat with graph-grounded citations), Capture (unified ingest: files, folders, web URL, browser extension, paste — merging today's Files view and the KG Capture tab), Memory, Automate (Agents/Workflows/Skills/Hooks/MCP behind Advanced), Settings/Admin. Decide the fate of the five hidden deep-link views (pipeline, planning, my-computer, marketplace, tools — routes.js:54-58): promote into the IA or delete; a 'hidden but maintained' third tier should not survive into v4. Move onboarding into the SPA as a first-run Capture flow.

opportunities.title: Vendor fonts and icons locally; rebuild the service worker for v3 offline
opportunities.detail: Ship Inter (woff2 subsets) and the Tabler icon font (or an SVG sprite of the ~60 icons actually used) under /static, drop the fonts.googleapis.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net links from v3/index.html and account.html. Regenerate sw.js at build time from asset-manifest.json so it precaches the exact hashed v3 assets with a cache name derived from package.json version — making 'no data leaves your computer' and offline-first actually true.

opportunities.title: Rebuild login/account as a v3-token surface
opportunities.detail: Replace account.html + css/reference/account.css (and its 4 sibling reference stylesheets) with a minimal token-native auth screen using lattice.tokens/base/components, in the SPA's visual language, bilingual (en/ko). This deletes the last consumer of css/reference/* and unifies the first impression with the product.

opportunities.title: Stop committing build artifacts; add manifest-consistency CI
opportunities.detail: Move hashed output to a gitignored static/v3/dist/ (or generate during release:artifacts only), and add a CI check that rebuilding produces a byte-identical asset-manifest.json — preventing the stale-hashed-asset failure mode entirely. The build script (scripts/build_v3_assets.mjs) already supports this; it is a packaging/policy change.

opportunities.title: Enforce the design system mechanically
opportunities.detail: Extend scripts/lint_v3.mjs to (1) fail on raw hex/rgb values in static/v3/css/* outside the two token files, (2) fail on inline style colors in view JS, and (3) run axe-core in the existing Playwright v3.spec.js pass for the Basic-mode routes. This converts the well-followed token convention into a guarantee for v4 contributors.

opportunities.title: Add first-class i18n (en/ko) to the SPA
opportunities.detail: A tiny dictionary module keyed off store state (the legacy chat already proved ko/en demand — chat.js:521-525 had a language toggle). Externalize the ~300 UI strings in v3 views, default to browser locale, and translate the invite-gate and error surfaces so the product is consistent for its actual (Korean-speaking) first users.
